page_summary:
This is the first half (pages 1 through 5) of a ten-page sequence from Folder 18 of Philip K. Dick's Exegesis, dated August 1978 -- roughly four and a half years after the initial 2-3-74 visionary experiences. No OCR text layer exists for these pages in this corpus, so their specific content cannot be reported. Their established context is archival rather than textual: Folder 18 falls within the Exegesis's mid-period composition, a stretch during which Dick had been writing continuously since 1974, developing and revising his metaphysical framework in a process of extended philosophical self-interrogation. The published Exegesis (edited by Pamela Jackson and Jonathan Lethem, 2011) draws on only a fraction of the full manuscript, making unpublished folders like this one -- if and when transcribed -- potentially significant for tracing how Dick's thinking evolved between 1974 and his death in 1982.

**Why it matters.** As an unpublished, untranscribed portion of Dick's mid-period Exegesis, this folder would be of considerable scholarly value if and when its content becomes accessible -- the published Exegesis represents only a curated selection of the full manuscript, and unpublished mid-1978 material could add to scholars' understanding of how Dick's metaphysical framework developed between the initial 2-3-74 experiences and his later, more systematic statements like Cosmogony and Cosmology.
